## What was submitted

**Pick: Yazaki — award, rank 1, with conditions.**

**Why it was the only option.** Five of the six bidders — Aptiv, Draexlmaier, Samvardhana Motherson, Lear and Sumitomo Electric — have no accepted entity match, no criterion values and no assessment. A supplier with no accepted match cannot be a pick, so the category had no competitive comparison to make and the weight vector did no discriminating work. I said that plainly rather than dressing a sole-source up as a contest won.

**Why the award is conditional.** Yazaki's own numbers are strong — compliance 100 with no disqualifying factors, media 70 off a single moderately flagged article — but that cleanliness is thin in two specific ways:

- **Ownership exposure is null, not good.** The graph records 18 owner edges; the returned window didn't include them. The criterion itself insists this is "not the same as an absent owner," and I refused to let the blank read as a pass.
- **The adverse evidence sits below the parent.** The family walk — itself truncated — surfaced high-level Chinese SOE ownership on a first-hop member, a high-level Sheffield Hallam forced-labour subtier factor on Xiaogan Yazaki Auto Parts, and elevated Xinjiang-origin subtier exposure on Yazaki Component Technology. None of that touches the parent's compliance score, which is exactly why the score alone would have misled.

Conditions attach to the pick: walk the owner edges, exclude Xiaogan from the harness BOM in writing, produce a UFLPA traceability pack, document the SOE position, and nominate the build location so the Section 232 question can actually resolve.

**Two limits worth your attention.** Proximity scores 0 from 10,209 km — but that measures a Tokyo head office, not a factory, so it says nothing about where harnesses would be built for a North American programme. And Japan's 72.5 country score rests entirely on one logistics indicator; all five governance dimensions were missing.

Yazaki's assessment passed evaluation with no unresolved objections, so there was no inherited dissent to disclose. The open questions I did raise are unresolved *inputs*, not unresolved disagreements.
